content.text:
Your fix works for the case you reported: `slugify('Hello,  World!')` now returns `hello-world`, and the existing slug test passes.

The new code turns every run of characters outside `a-z0-9` into one hyphen, then strips hyphens from the start and end. I ran it on some edge cases:

| Input | Output | |
|---|---|---|
| `Hello,  World!` | `hello-world` | ✅ the bug you reported |
| `  leading and trailing  ` | `leading-and-trailing` | ✅ |
| `a--b` | `a-b` | ✅ |
| `foo_bar` | `foo-bar` | ✅ |
| `C++ & C#` | `c-c` | ✅ fine, though some information is lost |
| `Café Déjà vu` | `caf-d-j-vu` | ⚠️ accented letters are dropped |
| `Ünïcödé` | `n-c-d` | ⚠️ |
| `日本語`, `!!!`, `""` | `""` | ⚠️ the slug comes out empty |

The old code just replaced spaces, so `café` stayed `café`. Your version deletes accented letters, which makes it worse for any input that isn't ASCII. If that matters to you, a common fix is to strip the accents first, so `Café` becomes `cafe` instead of `caf`:
```js
s.normalize('NFKD').replace(/[\u0300-\u036f]/g, '')
```
Input with no Latin letters at all, like `日本語`, will still give an empty slug. You'd need to decide whether that's acceptable or whether to fall back to something else.

**Tests:**
- `npm test` fails overall, but the failure is in `test/dates.test.js`, not your change. `quarter()` in `src/dates.js` returns a 0-based quarter (February → 0) while the test expects 1. That file isn't touched in your diff.
- The only slug test checks `Hello World`, so nothing tests the bug you fixed. I'd add a test for `'Hello,  World!'` → `'hello-world'` so it can't come back unnoticed. I can add that, or the accent handling, if you'd like.
